title: Incident readiness matrix and runbook synthesis
author: Jordan Kim
content:
Overview

This document synthesizes the canonical runbooks for high-impact services and provides a compact readiness matrix used to prioritize runbook coverage, on-call mentorship, and game-day simulations. It is intended for on-call engineers, SRE leads, and incident commanders who own restoration playbooks and training for the rotation.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-recovery for Sev1/Sev2 events by 30% via consolidated playbooks and targeted game-days.
- Ensure every service has a tested primary runbook, a fallback plan (compatible model variant or degraded-mode), and a responsible owner.
- Provide repeatable communication templates for customer-facing and internal status updates.

Key concepts
- Readiness Score (0-100): single numeric summarization of a service’s incident preparedness. Calculated from: runbook completeness (40%), SLO instrumentation & alerts (30%), recent test coverage (20%), owner availability (10%).
- Playbook Synthesis: canonical extraction of critical actions from team-specific runbooks into a one-page triage ladder.
- Escalation Ladders: explicit contacts and times-to-escalate (5m, 15m, 60m) for each class of incident.

Readiness Matrix (sample)

Service | Primary Owner | SLO (availability / p95) | Runbook status | Readiness Score
api-gateway | Platform API | 99.95% / p95 < 250ms | canonical + tested (2026-01-12) | 88
inference-runtime | Serving Runtime | 99.9% / p95 < 350ms | canonical, partial simulated test | 72
kv-cache | Redis-cluster | 99.99% / p95 < 50ms | legacy runbook, needs update | 58
router | Smart Router | 99.9% / p95 < 200ms | canonical + canary plan | 82

(When authoring, use this table and export regularly to the team dashboard.)

Service Triage Ladder (one-page synthesis)
Example: inference-runtime (high cost / customer impact)
1) Detect and score impact
   - Alert: inference-runtime.cpu_ready_ratio > 0.85 for 2m OR request-error-rate > 2% for 3m.
   - Immediate check: /observability/dashboards/runtime/overview -> continous_failures panel.
2) Containment (first 10 minutes)
   - Switch routing policy to fallback-model variant: `redwood-cli route set --policy degraded --service inference-runtime --duration 20m`
   - If GPU OOMs: temporarily set model.max_batch_size=1 via remote config service.
3) Mitigation (10-45 minutes)
   - Drain new requests from impacted pool: `kubectl cordon pod/<pod-name>` and `kubectl scale deployment inference-runtime --replicas 0` for affected ASG.
   - Redeploy last-known-good image: `helm upgrade --reuse-values inference-runtime ./charts/inference --set image.tag=v2026-01-22`
4) Recovery and verification
   - Run smoke harness: `scripts/smoke/inference_smoke.py --model small --n 50` (pass >=95% success).
   - Confirm p95 latency back under SLO for 10m window.
5) Post-incident actions
   - Create postmortem entry within 24h; link to runbook if gaps were found.

Decision thresholds and SLO breakpoints
- Green: error budget > 30% — follow standard incident cadence.
- Yellow: error budget between 5% and 30% — notify product and SRE leads; prepare mitigations.
- Red: error budget < 5% or any multi-region outage for >5 minutes — page engineering leadership and open an incident channel.

Escalation matrix (condensed)
- 0-5 minutes: on-call primary (page via PD)
- 5-20 minutes: on-call secondary (if unresolved)
- 20-60 minutes: service owner and SREEM (SRE escalation manager)
- 60+ minutes: engineering director and product owner; consider exec notification if customer impact is severe

Customer-facing status templates
- Initial status (first 20 minutes)
  Subject: Incident: [service] degraded — initial update
  Body: We are investigating elevated errors for [service]. Impact: a subset of API requests may fail or experience elevated latency. Affected regions: [us-west-2]. Actions under way: switching routing and validating fallback models. We will update within 30 minutes.

- Follow-up (30-90 minutes)
  Subject: Incident update: progress on [service]
  Body: We have applied a temporary routing policy to reduce failures and begun a targeted rollback to a known-good image. Error rates have dropped from X% to Y%. We continue validation and expect another update in 60 minutes.

- Resolution
  Subject: Incident resolved: [service]
  Body: The issue impacting [service] has been resolved. Root cause (preliminary): [brief]. Actions taken: [routing fallback, rollback, config change]. Next steps: a full post-incident review will be published in 48 hours. If you experienced customer-visible data loss, contact support at support@redwood.com.

Internal status channel templates
- Triage header: [INC-ID] [service] [sev] — short summary — owner: @user
- Short update cadence: 5m until containment, then 15m until stable, then 60m until recovery.

Runbook hygiene checklist (to keep readiness high)
- Owner assigned and on-call escalation lines declared.
- Runbook < 3 pages summary + detailed steps & rollback commands.
- Test harness that exercises the mitigation path present in CI.
- Playbook contains clear telemetry queries for impact scoring.
- Postmortem template link included at top of runbook.

On-call Rotation Mentorship program
- Pairing: new on-call engineers are paired with a mentor from SRE for first 90 days of rotation. Mentor responsibilities: review runbook with mentee within first week, run two shadow incidents, conduct a simulated restore together at week 4.
- Competency milestones: read-only access to incident channel -> small triage actions -> execute containment -> lead a canary rollback under supervision.
- Evaluation: at the end of each rotation, the mentor fills a short readiness assessment (pass/fail + notes). Failure triggers a remediation plan with extra game-days.

Game-day syllabus (90-minute template)
- Objective: validate runbook actions for top 3 readiness-score-lacking services.
- Roles: facilitator (SRE lead), incident commander, primary on-call, secondary on-call, customer comms, observer.
- Timeline: 10m brief, 30m simulated incident, 20m remediation & rollback, 30m after-action and capture of improvements.
- Deliverables: updated runbook snippet, action items with owners, updated playbook test cases.

Postmortem template (to paste into the PM doc)
- Title: [INC-ID] — short descriptive title
- Timeline: minute-by-minute summary of key events
- Impact: customers affected, regions, measurable metrics (error rate, requests lost, latency regression)
- Root cause: technical explanation and detection path
- Contributing factors: people/process/tech factors
- Resolution: steps taken to restore service
- Corrective actions: owner + ETA, verification steps, and follow-up game-day if applicable
- Severity rationale and learning notes

Example CLI and Observability snippets
- Check rolling restarts: `kubectl get pods -l app=inference-runtime -o wide`
- Grep recent errors in logs: `stern inference-runtime --since 1m | grep -i "OOM\|error\|failed"`
- Run smoke script in CI: `python tests/smoke/run_smoke.py --suite runtime_quick --repeat 3`

Configuration sample (YAML snippet to be placed in runbooks)
```yaml
alert_rules:
  - name: inference_high_error_rate
    expr: sum(rate(http_request_errors_total[2m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total[2m])) > 0.02
    severity: page
    runbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/inference-runtime
```
Governance and review cadence
- Quarterly runbook audit: owners must update runbook and score on readiness matrix.
- After any Sev1 incident, the implicated runbook must be updated within 7 days; if not, an SRE lead escalates to engineering director.
- Game-days schedule: every team should run at least two focused game-days per year; teams with readiness score <70 must run an additional game-day.

Appendix: quick references
- Runbook location convention: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/<service-name>
- PagerDuty escalation policy: Redwood-Core-Oncall (primary -> secondary -> SREEM)
- Slack incident channel naming: #incident-<service>-<INC-ID>

If you are an on-call engineer and notice any missing item in the readiness matrix, file a `runbook-update` ticket under the SRE board and tag the service owner.

End of document
